evals.name: new-repo
evals.prompt: I need a supporting-information repo for our paper 'Ion-specific swelling of polyelectrolyte gels' (accepted in Soft Matter, DOI 10.1039/d6sm00123a). Authors: Anna Berg (ORCID 0000-0002-1825-0097, Lund University) and Erik Lind (Uppsala University). It'll hold Python notebooks using numpy and scipy. Create it at {OUT}/gel-swelling-si.
evals.expected_output: A repo scaffolded from the template with consistent metadata, scipy added via uv, and missing items asked rather than invented.
assertions: Repository has pyproject.toml, uv.lock, .zenodo.json, CITATION.cff and AGENTS.md
scipy and numpy are dependencies in pyproject.toml and uv.lock
ruff check and pytest pass in the new repository
.zenodo.json lists both authors and Anna Berg's ORCID, and the paper DOI as isSupplementTo
.zenodo.json passes Zenodo's legacy schema (e.g. no 'language' field)
CITATION.cff agrees with .zenodo.json on title and authors
No ORCID is invented for Erik Lind
Missing information (Erik Lind's ORCID, license, funding) is listed as questions
License is not changed from the template without the user's confirmation, and is asked about in QUESTIONS.md with a recommendation

evals.name: adapt-messy-dir
evals.prompt: Turn my project in {IN}/adapt-messy-dir into supporting information for the paper described in its notes.txt, ready for Zenodo. Put the new repository at {OUT}/lyso-si.
evals.expected_output: Original untouched; new repo from the template; duplicated rdf code turned into one tested module; trajectory kept out of git with a deposit plan; questions for missing metadata.
assertions: The original directory is unchanged
The new repository is separate and has the template layout (pyproject.toml, uv.lock, src/, tests/, notebooks/)
A source-to-destination mapping of the original files is given
The duplicated rdf function lives once in src/ and both figure drivers import it
Tests cover the rdf function, including one pinning its current output
No absolute /home/jane paths remain in the new repository
ruff check and pytest pass in the new repository
md.xtc is not committed to git, and a deposit plan for it (or for extracted features instead) is given
Missing information (ORCIDs, license) is listed as questions, not invented
License is not decided unilaterally: asked about with a recommendation, and flagged as unconfirmed
If code and data licenses are split, the .zenodo.json description states which license covers what

evals.name: review-flawed-repo
evals.prompt: We're about to release {IN}/review-flawed-repo on Zenodo. Review it and tell me what to fix. Don't change anything.
evals.expected_output: A read-only report ranked by impact with concrete fixes.
assertions: The reviewed directory is unchanged
Flags that .zenodo.json's 'language' field is rejected by Zenodo's schema
Flags the title mismatch between README and .zenodo.json
Flags missing ORCID or 'Family, Given' creator format
Flags missing related publication DOI
Flags environment.yml without pinned versions or lock file
Flags the GitHub action pinned to @main
Flags CC-BY as a license for code
Flags the absolute path in the notebook
Flags missing CITATION.cff
Findings are ranked by impact and each has a concrete fix
